subject: Marketplace SKU routing & entitlement decision for CloudBridge listing

From: Sasha Martin <sasha@cloudbridge.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace SKU routing & entitlement proposal

Hi Ava / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the potential to list CloudBridge’s observability connectors in Redwood’s catalog and take advantage of co-sell routing for mutual customers. Attached is an initial SKU mapping (CloudBridge_SKU_mapping_v1.xlsx) showing our current products, suggested SKU names for AWS/GCP listings, and the tenancy models (self-serve vs. managed).

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether these SKUs can be routed as co-sell eligible vs. reseller-only?
- What evidence is required (technical & commercial) to be marked for co-sell in Azure/GCP catalogs?
- Any blockers from entitlements / meter mapping that we should address now?

We’re hoping to pick 3 pilot SKUs for the initial launch and then expand. Happy to jump on a quick call — looking for a decision on routing policy and a short list of evidence items.

Attachments: CloudBridge_SKU_mapping_v1.xlsx (excel)

Best,
Sasha Martin
Partnerships, CloudBridge
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU routing & entitlement proposal

Hi Sasha — thanks for the mapping and context, this is helpful. I looped in Ben (alliances), Karthik (partner eng) and Monica (legal ops) so we can triage across catalog, technical evidence and contracting. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Routing decision scope — we typically evaluate co-sell eligibility based on three things:
   - Technical integration & support model (is product deployable in customer environment / managed by partner)
   - Commercial commitments (co-sell agreement / margin/discount commitments)
   - Metering / SKU mapping compatibility per cloud (some clouds require publisher meter conformity)

2) For a minimal pilot we recommend 3 SKUs (one self-serve, one managed, one hybrid). Can you flag which three you want to start with?

3) Evidence checklist (initial):
   - Deployment guide / architecture diagram (PDF)
   - One customer reference + PoC notes (contact + summary)
   - Co-sell commitment PDF or LOI that shows go-to-market commit
   - SKU meter mapping (CSV) for each cloud

Karthik — can you review the attachment and call out any technical gating items for GCP marketplace (e.g., meter format, service account flows)?
Ben — can you own the commercial routing decision and coordinate with marketplace PMs?
Monica — once Sasha shares the co-sell commitment draft we’ll want a quick legal review.

Sasha — if you can send the deployment guide and the co-sell commitment by EOD today we’ll aim to get an initial routing decision by end of week and schedule a sync with the marketplace teams.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

Thanks Ava — attached are the items requested: CB_sku_matrix.csv and CloudBridge_co-sell-commitment.pdf. We’ve also added a short deployment guide (one-pager) into the Drive link below.

Pilot SKUs we propose:
- CB-OBS-S (self-serve observability connector)
- CB-OBS-M (managed connector)
- CB-OBS-H (hybrid; self-serve with optional managed onboarding)

Notes on metering: our current meter schema is column-based (see CSV). We know Azure has a stricter SKU/Meter format; happy to adapt. For GCP we already have a partner-provider integration in staging.

We can do a quick 30m call at 3pm PT if that works for you to walk through the matrix and agree on who owns what.

Attachments: CB_sku_matrix.csv (csv), CloudBridge_co-sell-commitment.pdf (pdf)
